title: Tunable priority funnel for quantization and routing consults
creator: Linnea Chen
description: Design and deliver a configurable intake + scoring funnel for optimization/advisory requests focused on batching/caching knobs, quantization profiles, and routing policies. Objective: reduce time-to-first-response for enterprise customers, ensure SLA-aware routing to the right responder (self-serve guidance, Optimize team, or SRE/field engineering), and produce a prioritized queue that balances latency SLO risk, cost-savings potential, and customer business impact.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form produced in Console prototype with fields for workload signals (p50/p95 latency, token/sec), cost sensitivity, model family, deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), and compliance constraints
Scoring algorithm implemented as a lightweight service (priority score output 0-100) documented with weighting defaults and override knobs
Routing rules created: auto-self-serve (score < 30), Optimize triage (30-70), Enterprise escalation (>=70) with SLA targets for response times
Playbook and runbook added to Confluence with sample diagnosis steps for batching, KV cache tuning, quantization suggestions, and routing fallbacks
Telemetry events emitted for every intake (source, score, route) and dashboards added to Console to monitor backlog and latency to first response
tasks: Draft intake form fields and validations with UX (Design)
Define scoring features and default weights (PM + Applied ML)
Implement simple scoring service and webhook to route to Slack/Queue (ENG)
Create Console prototype for intake and attach links to customer artifacts
Write playbook items and consensus decision for enterprise overrides
Wire telemetry events and build monitoring dashboard (Observability)
Run 4-week pilot with top-10 enterprise customers and capture SLA metrics
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive cost-weighting favors batch/quant suggestions but risks model quality regressions; plan to gate high-impact quant suggestions behind manual review for enterprise customers.
We should prioritize requests tied to measurable SLO breaches (p95 spikes) and requests that estimate >20% unit-cost reduction.
Design constraint: the intake must be minimal (3-5 required fields) to avoid blocking customers; advanced fields hidden under 'advanced config'.
Consider exposing a read-only version of the score to customers for transparency and to guide self-serve fixes.

implementation_risks: Automated quant suggestions could introduce model-quality regressions if eval gating is incomplete
Inaccurate customer-provided signals (noisy p95/p50) may skew the score; need validation rules and optional agent-assisted capture
Routing policies must handle multi-tenant Dedicated instances where data residency prevents automated telemetry ingestion
